case.label: Community-acquired pneumonia
case.chief_complaint: Cough and fever for three days
exam: Patient appears unwell, diaphoretic, and in mild respiratory distress. Is sitting upright and leaning forward to facilitate breathing. Appears anxious and fatigued.
Vital signs: Temp 39.0°C (102.2°F), HR 105 bpm, RR 22 breaths/min, BP 120/80 mmHg, SpO2 94% on room air.

Respiratory examination reveals use of accessory muscles with mild intercostal retractions. Bilateral crackles are heard at the lung bases. Breath sounds are diminished in the lower lobes bilaterally. No wheezing or rhonchi are present. The patient is tachypne
Cardiovascular examination reveals a regular rate and rhythm with no palpable thrills or murmurs. No jugular venous distension is noted. Peripheral pulses are 2+ and symmetric. No edema is present.
